meta_title: Online shopping with arthritis and frailty (UK)
meta_description: Tips for shopping online for food and essentials when arthritis and frailty make shops hard: priority slots, easy packaging, and meals and drinks.
excerpt: Tips for shopping online for food and essentials when arthritis and frailty make shops hard: priority slots, easy packaging, and meals and drinks.
direct_answer: Online shopping can reduce lifting, walking and queues. Some supermarkets offer priority slots. Choose easy-open packaging, smaller items, and plan meals and drinks. Ask a family member or volunteer if you need help setting up.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
Shopping can be tiring with sore hands and joints. Online shopping can help.

This guide covers practical tips. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Getting started

  • Ask family or a local volunteer for help.
  • Use large text settings.
  • Save a regular list.

Delivery

  • Ask about priority slots.
  • Ask drivers to bring bags inside if possible.
  • Choose lighter bags.

Food and fluid

  • Keep easy meals and snacks.
  • Choose drinks you can open.
  • Include protein foods.

Easier packaging

  • Ready-chopped vegetables.
  • Ring-pull tins.
  • Smaller bottles.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is online shopping safe?

Use trusted sites.

What if I cannot use a computer?

Phone orders or volunteers may help.
